SKILLS
convertSpeed — Convert a speed — miles per hour, kilometres per hour, metres per second, knots.
  needs: amount: number, from: string, to: string
  e.g. "100 km/h in mph" → {"amount":100,"from":"km/h","to":"mph"}
convertLength — Convert a distance or length — millimetres, centimetres, metres, kilometres, inches, feet, yards, miles.
  needs: amount: number, from: string, to: string
  e.g. "how many km is 26.2 miles" → {"amount":26.2,"from":"miles","to":"km"}
convertFuelEconomy — Convert fuel economy between litres per 100km, miles per gallon and kilometres per litre.
  needs: amount: number, from: string, to: string
  e.g. "convert 30 mpg to litres per 100km" → {"amount":30,"from":"mpg","to":"l/100km"}
convertAngle — Convert an angle — degrees, radians, gradians, turns, arcminutes, arcseconds.
  needs: amount: number, from: string, to: string
  e.g. "convert 180 degrees to radians" → {"amount":180,"from":"degrees","to":"radians"}
convertArea — Convert an area — square metres, square feet, hectares, acres, square miles.
  needs: amount: number, from: string, to: string
  e.g. "how many square feet is 85 square metres" → {"amount":85,"from":"m2","to":"ft2"}
convertDataSize — Convert a file or storage size — bytes, kB, MB, GB, TB, and the binary KiB, MiB, GiB.
  needs: amount: number, from: string, to: string
  e.g. "how many GiB is 500 GB" → {"amount":500,"from":"GB","to":"GiB"}
convertMass — Convert a weight or mass — grams, kilograms, tonnes, ounces, pounds, stone.
  needs: amount: number, from: string, to: string
  e.g. "what is 70 kg in stone" → {"amount":70,"from":"kg","to":"stone"}
convertRomanNumeral — Convert a number to Roman numerals, or read Roman numerals back as a number.
  needs: value: string
  e.g. "what is 2026 in roman numerals" → {"value":"2026"}
convertTemperature — Convert a temperature between Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin.
  needs: amount: number, from: string, to: string
  e.g. "convert 180 celsius to fahrenheit" → {"amount":180,"from":"celsius","to":"fahrenheit"}
numberToWords — Write a number out in words, the way it would be spoken or written on a cheque.
  needs: value: number
  optional: style: string, currency: string
  e.g. "write 1234 in words" → {"value":1234}

MESSAGE
100 km/h in mph
{"about":"convert a speed","steps":[{"id":"s1","skill":"convertSpeed","input":{"amount":100,"from":"km/h","to":"mph"}}]}

SKILLS
percentOf — Take a percentage of a number — 15% of 240, or 20 percent of a bill.
  needs: percent: number, value: number
  e.g. "what is 15% of 240" → {"percent":15,"value":240}
whatPercent — Given a part and a total, work out what share the part is — 36 out of 240, or a score out of a maximum.
  needs: part: number, whole: number
  e.g. "36 out of 240 as a percentage" → {"part":36,"whole":240}
percentChange — Percentage change between two numbers, and the difference in plain terms.
  needs: from: number, to: number
  e.g. "my rent went from 1200 to 1350, what percent increase is that" → {"from":1200,"to":1350}
fibonacci — Give the nth Fibonacci number, or the first n of them.
  needs: n: integer
  optional: mode: string
  e.g. "what is the 10th fibonacci number" → {"n":10}

  optional: style: string
  e.g. "write 1234.5 as pounds" → {"amount":1234.5,"currency":"GBP"}
formatNumber — Write a number with thousands separators, a set number of decimals, or in compact form like 1.2k.
  needs: value: number
  optional: decimals: integer, style: string

fractionSimplify — Reduce a fraction to its lowest terms.
  needs: fraction: string
  e.g. "simplify 6/8" → {"fraction":"6/8"}
gcd — Find the greatest common divisor — the largest number that divides a set of whole numbers exactly.

  needs: value: integer

  needs: values: array
  e.g. "lowest common multiple of 4 and 6" → {"values":[4,6]}

  needs: text: string
  e.g. "what number is 1.2k" → {"text":"1.2k"}
primeFactors — Break a whole number down into the prime numbers it is made of.
  needs: value: integer
  e.g. "prime factors of 360" → {"value":360}
product — Multiply a list of numbers together.
  needs: values: array
  e.g. "multiply 12 by 8 by 3" → {"values":[12,8,3]}
roundTo — Round a number to a number of decimal places or significant figures.
  needs: value: number, places: integer
  optional: mode: string
  e.g. "round 3.14159 to 2 decimal places" → {"value":3.14159,"places":2}

  needs: from: number, to: number

  e.g. "list the numbers 1 to 5" → {"from":1,"to":5}
differenceLists — Find what is in one list but not the other, in both directions.
  needs: first: array, second: array
  optional: ignoreCase: boolean
  e.g. "what is in the first list but not the second" → {"first":["a","b","c"],"second":["b"]}
chunkList — Split a list into smaller groups of a fixed size.
  needs: items: array, size: integer

  needs: items: array
  optional: ignoreCase: boolean
  e.g. "count how many of each are in this list" → {"items":["red","blue","red","green","red"]}
dedupeList — Remove repeated items from a list, keeping the first of each and the original order.
  needs: items: array
  optional: ignoreCase: boolean
  e.g. "remove the duplicates from this list" → {"items":["apple","banana","apple","cherry"]}
flattenList — Flatten a list of nested lists into a single flat list.
  needs: items: array
  optional: depth: integer
  e.g. "flatten this nested list" → {"items":[1,[2,3],[4,[5]]]}
intersectLists — Find the items that appear in both of two lists.
  needs: first: array, second: array
  optional: ignoreCase: boolean
  e.g. "what is in both of these lists" → {"first":["apple","banana","cherry"],"second":["banana","cherry","date"]}

pickRandom — Pick one or more items at random from a list, from a seed so the pick can be repeated.
  needs: items: array, seed: integer
  optional: count: integer, allowRepeats: boolean
  e.g. "pick one of these at random with seed 7" → {"items":["tea","coffee","water"],"seed":7}
sortList — Put a list of items in order — alphabetically, numerically, or in natural order where numbers inside names count.
  needs: items: array
  optional: by: string, direction: string
  e.g. "sort this list alphabetically" → {"items":["cherry","apple","banana"]}
unionLists — Combine two lists into one, keeping each item once.
  needs: first: array, second: array
  optional: ignoreCase: boolean
  e.g. "combine these two lists" → {"first":["a","b"],"second":["b","c"]}
zipLists — Combine two or more lists position by position into grouped rows.
  needs: lists: array
  optional: names: array, strict: boolean
  e.g. "zip these two lists together" → {"lists":[[1,2,3],["a","b","c"]]}
